The chapter is VSAQ-only: it prints 24 Very Short Answer Questions and has no Short Answer and no Long Answer section at all, and no PROBLEMS. Neither the two-book union check nor a board back-test was possible for Chemistry-II: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is physics-only and first-year, and no second-year chemistry paper is in the corpus. The chemistry is correct and is kept; the broken grammar is rewritten. GAP: the book gives no monomers for its examples, and names polyesters only as a class; the monomers of nylon-6,6 and terylene are supplied.

steps.why: Strong forces between neighbouring chains are what let a thread carry a load without the chains sliding apart, and the same forces hold the chains in a regular, crystalline arrangement. That is the exact opposite of the weak forces that make an elastomer.
common_mistakes: Writing that fibre chains are held by weak forces. Weak forces give an elastomer; fibres need strong ones.
Leaving out the hydrogen bonding. It is what the structure half of this mark is given for.
steps.memory_tip: Strong forces between chains give a fibre; weak forces give an elastomer.
steps.margin_note: Thread forming, high tensile strength and strong intermolecular forces are the three items in this mark.

steps.why: Both examples carry a polar link in every repeat unit, an amide in nylon and an ester in terylene, so neighbouring chains attract strongly all along their length. A fibre is not a separate kind of chemistry; it is a polymer whose links line up between chains.
common_mistakes: Giving polythene as a fibre. Its chain has no polar group, so the forces between chains are weak.
Naming a fibre without its monomers. The monomers are where the marks are in this chapter.
steps.memory_tip: Both standard fibres are condensation polymers with a polar link in every repeat unit.
steps.margin_note: Two named fibres finish this mark. Nylon-6,6 and terylene are the pair the book prints.

insider_note: The examiner looks for thread forming, high tensile strength and strong intermolecular forces. The example is usually nylon-6,6.
